questions.q: What does “defensive driving” mean?
options: Driving as slowly as possible in every situation
Driving on the assumption that someone else might make a mistake, and being ready for it in advance
Driving suited only to very experienced drivers
Focusing only on your own rights on the road
questions.explain: Defensive driving is an approach of anticipating other people’s mistakes in advance, not a slow or fearful driving style.

questions.q: Why isn’t right of way at a junction a real “protection” against a crash?
options: Because right of way only applies to heavy vehicles
Because another vehicle might still not stop, regardless of the legal right
Because right of way changes every day
Because right of way doesn’t exist in Israeli law
questions.explain: Even when the law is on your side, another vehicle might not respect the right of way - so you drive so that you’ll have time to react.

questions.q: What is a space cushion?
options: A distance you’re allowed to exceed the speed limit by
Open space around the car on every side, giving you time and options if something goes wrong
An extra airbag in the car
Another name for a seatbelt
questions.explain: A space cushion is the space kept ahead, behind and to the sides - the bigger it is, the more time you have to react.

questions.q: A driver is driving at the speed limit, in their own lane, with a green light in their favour. What does the defensive driving approach suggest?
options: Stop at every junction even with a green light
Stop scanning, because their right is clear
Speed up to cross faster, since the light is in their favour
Enter the junction at a pace that allows a reaction, and scan to the sides despite the green light
questions.explain: Even with a green light, you scan to the sides, because another vehicle might not stop at their red light.

questions.q: Why is it important to look far beyond the vehicle right in front of you?
options: Only to choose a faster lane
To read advertising signs in time
To spot braking, an obstacle or a change in traffic early
Because it’s forbidden to look at the vehicle right in front
questions.explain: Looking far ahead, beyond the vehicle right in front, spots changes in traffic long before they reach you.

questions.q: About how often should you check the mirrors and dashboard while driving normally?
options: Once a minute only
Every few seconds, in a quick glance that returns to the road at once
Only at the start of the drive
Only when planning to turn
questions.explain: Frequent, brief checks keep an up-to-date picture of your surroundings, without taking your eyes off the road for long.

questions.q: What is the blind spot in a car?
options: Only the area behind the car, visible in the rear-view mirror
An area you can see well only in the side mirror
An area around the car that isn’t visible in the mirrors or in direct sight, mainly to the rear-side
Any area outside the car
questions.explain: The blind spot is exactly the area the mirrors don’t cover - another vehicle can travel there without you knowing.

questions.q: Before changing lanes, what must you do beyond checking the mirror?
options: Turn on the hazard lights
Speed up to get past quickly
Turn your head and check the blind spot directly
Honk to warn other vehicles
questions.explain: The mirror alone doesn’t cover the blind spot - you must turn your head and check directly before changing lanes.

questions.q: Why does the scanning pattern matter even on the most familiar road?
options: Because it’s exactly on a familiar road that it’s easy to “switch off” and stop really scanning
Because a familiar road has more hazards than a new one
Because the mirrors don’t work normally on a familiar road
It doesn’t matter - you can skip scanning on a familiar road
questions.explain: Routine dulls alertness; a consistent scanning pattern keeps the same level of attention even on the most familiar road.

questions.q: You see a ball rolling into the road from a playground. What is the right thing to do?
options: Speed up to get past before anyone runs out
Honk continuously until you pass the spot
Ignore it, because the ball itself isn’t dangerous
Slow down and prepare for the chance that a child will run after the ball
questions.explain: A rolling ball is a classic sign warning that a child may run after it into the road.

questions.q: Why should you be especially careful near a bus stopped at a stop?
options: Because buses always drive too fast
It may hide a pedestrian crossing in front of or behind it
Because a bus always turns left near a stop
Because you can never overtake a bus
questions.explain: A stopped bus can hide a pedestrian crossing near it - slow down and stay alert.

questions.q: The brake lights of a vehicle far ahead of you are flashing, even though the vehicle right in front of you hasn’t slowed yet. What is correct?
options: Treat it as a sign that traffic may be about to slow down, and prepare
Ignore it, because it doesn’t concern the vehicle right in front of you
Speed up so you can overtake before traffic slows down
It’s always a technical fault in the distant vehicle
questions.explain: Distant brake lights are an early clue that all the traffic ahead may be about to slow down - it’s better to prepare in advance.

questions.q: Why is it wrong to assume that a pedestrian looking at their phone at the roadside notices your car?
options: Because they’re busy with their phone and might cross without paying attention to traffic
Because this is only true at night
Because pedestrians always see well, regardless of a phone
Because the law forbids pedestrians from using a phone
questions.explain: A pedestrian absorbed in their phone might not notice the traffic - a careful driver doesn’t assume they see them.

questions.q: What is the most common cause of a rear-end collision?
options: Too short a gap from the vehicle in front, or too late a reaction
Driving with the lights on during the day
An airbag fault
Driving too slowly for the traffic
questions.explain: A rear-end collision happens almost always because of too short a gap or too late a reaction - a space cushion ahead prevents it.

questions.q: What is the main prevention principle against a head-on collision?
options: Always drive with high beams on
When in doubt whether the oncoming lane is clear enough for overtaking - don’t overtake
Always overtake at the highest possible speed
Always drive on the left side of the road
questions.explain: A head-on collision usually happens from a dangerous overtake - when in doubt about the oncoming lane, simply don’t overtake.

questions.q: Why isn’t right of way at a junction enough to avoid a crash?
options: Because right of way changes at every junction
Because it’s forbidden to enter a junction on a green light
Because right of way only applies during the day
Because a vehicle entering from the other direction might not stop, even without right of way
questions.explain: Right of way is a legal rule, not a guarantee the other side will actually stop - enter the junction carefully.

questions.q: The wheels of the car have drifted slightly onto the shoulder. What is the correct action?
options: Yank the wheel sharply back onto the road
Brake hard immediately
Ease off the accelerator slightly, hold the wheel steady and return to the lane gently
Speed up to get back into the lane faster
questions.explain: A sharp correction can send the car across the whole road to the other side - bring it back gently and gradually.

questions.q: What do the common crashes - rear-end, head-on, running off the road - have in common?
options: They’re only linked to vehicle faults
All of them are far easier to prevent before they start, with a suitable distance and speed
They only happen at night
They are completely unavoidable
questions.explain: In all of these patterns, early prevention - distance, speed and scanning - works far better than a last-moment fix.

questions.q: What is the most common root cause of a skid?
options: Newly fitted brakes
Tyres that are too new
Hot weather at too high a temperature
A speed unsuited to the bend or the road conditions
questions.explain: Most skids are a direct result of a speed unsuited to the bend or the road conditions.

questions.q: In a car that turns less than expected in a bend, with the front wheels sliding wide, what is the correct fix?
options: Turn the wheel even harder
Brake hard in the middle of the turn
Ease off the accelerator and look where you want to go
Speed up to “push” the car into the turn
questions.explain: This is understeer; easing off the accelerator and looking in the desired direction helps the front wheels regain grip.

questions.q: What does electronic stability control (ESC) do in a skid?
options: Replaces the need for careful driving
Increases the car’s speed to get out of the skid
Automatically brakes individual wheels to help the car return to the intended direction
Disconnects the engine completely
questions.explain: ESC brakes individual wheels to reduce sideways skidding and help maintain direction.

questions.q: Why is it wrong to rely on ESC instead of a suitable speed?
options: Because ESC doesn’t exist in private cars
Because ESC only works on a dry road
Because ESC only works below 30 km/h
Because ESC doesn’t create grip that isn’t there - it doesn’t cancel the laws of physics
questions.explain: ESC helps maintain direction, but it can’t create grip that doesn’t exist - a suitable speed for the conditions remains the basis.

questions.q: When should you turn on the indicator before a turn or a lane change?
options: Exactly the moment you start turning
No need if the lane is completely clear
Only if there’s another vehicle in the blind spot
Early, before starting the manoeuvre - not in the middle of it
questions.explain: An early signal gives other drivers time to react calmly, instead of having to correct at the last moment.

questions.q: A vehicle is trying to merge from a lane that’s ending. What is the correct behaviour?
options: Leave it space and allow the merge
Stick close to the vehicle ahead so as not to give it room
Honk until it gives way
Speed up to block it
questions.explain: Giving space for a merge costs a few seconds and prevents the pressured situations that cause mistakes.

questions.q: Another driver lets you into a lane. What is correct?
options: You must stop and thank them in person
You must wait at least a minute before continuing
It’s forbidden to thank them in any way
You can thank them with a brief flash of the hazard lights when it’s safe, without stopping in traffic
questions.explain: A brief, safe thank-you is accepted, but it’s a nice extra - not a reason to stop in the middle of traffic.
